chunks: So he said: “May Allah brighten a servant who hears my statement, then comprehends it, preserves it, and conveys it to one who did not hear it. For perhaps a bearer of fiqh is not himself a faqih, and perhaps a bearer of fiqh conveys it to one who is more understanding than him.”

There are three things concerning which the heart of a Muslim man does not act treacherously: sincerity of action for Allah, sincere counsel toward the Imams of the Muslims, and adherence to their community, for their call encompasses those behind them.
The Muslims are brothers; their blood is equal, and the least of them may uphold their covenant.

And it was also narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Abān, from Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, similarly; and it adds: “and they are one hand against those besides them.” And he mentioned in his hadith that he delivered the sermon during the Farewell Hajj at Minā in Masjid al-Khayf.

key_terms.أَئِمَّةِ: The Imams or leaders of the Muslims, toward whom sincere counsel is due.
key_terms.إِخْلَاصُ: Sincerity; making one's deed purely for Allah.
key_terms.جَمَاعَتِهِمْ: Their community or united body, whose cohesion is to be maintained.
key_terms.ذِمَّتِهِمْ: Their covenant, guarantee, or protected commitment upheld on behalf of the Muslims.
key_terms.فِقْهٍ: Religious understanding or transmitted knowledge of religion.
key_terms.مَقَالَتِي: My statement or teaching; the prophetic instruction being heard and conveyed.
key_terms.نَضَّرَ: May Allah brighten or grace; a supplication for one who faithfully receives and transmits the teaching.

ai.seo_question: What did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم teach about sincerity, the Imams of the Muslims, and the unity of the Muslim community?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes preserving and transmitting the teachings of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, even when the transmitter may not fully grasp all their depths. It also identifies three foundations of upright communal religion: sincerity for Allah, sincere counsel toward the Imams of the Muslims, and remaining with their community. The report concludes by affirming Muslim brotherhood, mutual protection, and collective solidarity.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Aban Bin Usman, from Ibn Abu Yafour,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>azwj</sup> addressed the people in Masjid Al-Kheif, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Flourish (Grant Joy and Happiness) the servant who hears my<sup>asws</sup> speech, so he retains it and preserves it and delivers it to the one who did not hear it. Sometimes a bearer’s understanding is other than his (the transmitter’s) understanding, and sometimes a bearer would be of more understanding than him (the transmitter).

There are three upon which a Muslim’s heart of a Muslim does not feel greed/envy – Sincerity of the deed for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the advice of the Imams<sup>asws</sup> of the Muslims, and the necessitation to their<sup>asws</sup> gatherings, for their<sup>asws</sup> invitation encompasses from behind them.
The Muslims are brothers, their bloods are a match for each other, and their lowest one strives for their responsibilities’.

And it is reported as well, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Aban, from Ibn Abu Yafour, similar to it, and there is an increase in it, (He<sup>saww</sup> said): ‘And they are one hand to face their enemies’, and he mentioned in his Hadeeth that he<sup>saww</sup> addressed during the farewell Hajj at Mina in Masjid Al-Kheif.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from Aban ibnn ‘Uthman from ibn abu Ya‘fur from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “The the Messenger of Allah addressed people in the mosque of Khif

and said, “May Allah grant joy and happiness to those of His servants that on hearing my words understand them, memorize them preach them to those who have not heard them. There can be many scholars of Fiqh (law) who do not have understanding as there can be many bearers of Fiqh (law) to those who are better scholars of Fiqh (law) then the bearer.

There are three things in which the heart of a Muslim does not feel greed and treachery. Sincerity in deeds for Allah, wishing well for the leaders of the Muslims and to stay close with the group of the Muslims because their prayer encompass them from behind them
and the Muslims are each other’s brothers. Their lives are as each other’s lives and the least important among them strive to fulfill their responsibilities.”

Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from Aban from ibn abu Ya‘fur has narrated a similar hadith with an addition of “They are as one hand to face their enemies”. In his Hadith he has mentioned that the Holy Prophet (s.a) made his speech during his farewell pilgrimage in the mosque of Khif.
